summary: Stores user-defined numeric measurement series, each named by a LabelEngine label, and exposes list, detail, and batch API surfaces for tracking values over time.

classification.why_application: Owns domain rules for measurement entries (one numeric value + timestamp per entry), enforces series lifecycle (label + measurements), and determines what constitutes a 'latest value', 'sparkline', and 'series history' for a specific user-facing product loop.
non_goals: Alerts, targets, trends, insights, or anomaly detection
Rich charting beyond sparkline and detail history
classification.not_platform: The measurement lifecycle, sparkline derivation, and series-read API are specific to this product's tracking domain. No other application consumes these behaviors. Promoting them to platform would encode application-specific meaning in a shared service.

consumes: LabelEngine HTTP API: POST /api/labels (create label), GET /api/labels (search labels)
LabelEngine Postgres shared schema: labels.labels table (read label name by id)
02_Platform/packages: platform_contracts (Dataset, DatasetMeta, ColumnSchema), platform_errorhandling (api_error, logging, FastAPI handlers)
provides: List of all series with sparkline and latest value (sorted by label name)
Full measurement history for a single series (editable)
Batch read of multiple series with their measurements (external API for OpenClaw)
Add measurements for an existing label (external API for OpenClaw)
invariants: Every measurement entry has exactly one numeric value and one timestamp
Latest value is always derived from the measurement with the most recent recorded_at
A label can exist with zero measurements
Deleting a series removes all its measurement entries
Label names are managed exclusively through LabelEngine; NumericSeries never creates label name strings independently
Batch read returns a result entry for every requested label_id, including empty series; full measurement history is returned for each series (no windowing)
failure_modes: LABEL_NOT_FOUND: label_id referenced by a write does not exist in LabelEngine
MEASUREMENT_NOT_FOUND: measurement id not found or does not belong to the given label
SERIES_NOT_FOUND: label_id has no series record (not tracked by NumericSeries)
LABEL_ENGINE_UNAVAILABLE: LabelEngine HTTP call fails; label creation/search blocked
INVALID_VALUE: measurement value is not a valid finite number
INVALID_TIMESTAMP: recorded_at cannot be parsed as ISO-8601

consumes: LabelEngine HTTP: POST /api/labels — create label when user names a new series
LabelEngine HTTP: GET /api/labels?q= — search/autocomplete label names
LabelEngine Postgres: labels.labels — joined for label name on list queries
provides: GET  /api/series             — list all series (label name, sparkline data, latest value)
POST /api/series             — create a new series (creates label via LabelEngine, registers series)
GET  /api/series/{label_id}  — detail: full measurement history for a label
DELETE /api/series/{label_id} — delete series and all its measurements
PATCH /api/series/{label_id}/measurements/{id}  — edit a measurement (value and/or timestamp)
POST /api/batch/series       — batch read: return measurements for a list of label_ids
POST /api/series/{label_id}/values — external write: add one or more measurements for OpenClaw

exposed_surfaces.name: GET /api/series
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Returns all tracked series sorted by label name. The response is a Dataset where sparkline_values is encoded as a JSON string (ColumnType: 'string') so that the UI Data Contract's closed ColumnType set is not violated. The SeriesListPage frontend component must parse sparkline_values and render the sparkline — standard platform TableView is not suitable for this surface; a custom list component is required.
exposed_surfaces.ui_contract: Dataset | ApiError — sparkline_values column type: 'string' (JSON-encoded float array); NOT rendered by standard TableView

exposed_surfaces.name: POST /api/series
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Creates a new series: calls LabelEngine to create the label, inserts a series record.

exposed_surfaces.name: GET /api/series/{label_id}
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Returns full measurement history for the series as a Dataset, sorted by recorded_at DESC.

exposed_surfaces.name: DELETE /api/series/{label_id}
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Deletes the series record and all its measurements. Does not delete the label from LabelEngine.

exposed_surfaces.name: POST /api/series/{label_id}/measurements
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Adds a new measurement entry to the series.

exposed_surfaces.name: PATCH /api/series/{label_id}/measurements/{id}
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Edits an existing measurement entry (value and/or recorded_at).

exposed_surfaces.name: POST /api/batch/series
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Batch read: accepts a list of label_ids and returns each with its full measurement history including empty series.
exposed_surfaces.ui_contract: none — external contract for OpenClaw; returns {series: [{label_id, label_name, measurements: [{id, value, recorded_at}]}]}

exposed_surfaces.name: POST /api/series/{label_id}/values
exposed_surfaces.purpose: External write endpoint for OpenClaw: accepts one or more {value, recorded_at} entries and appends them to the series.
exposed_surfaces.ui_contract: none — external contract; returns {inserted: int} | ApiError

internal_flow.name: label_creation
internal_flow.description: When a user creates a new series, the backend calls LabelEngine POST /api/labels with the desired name. On success it receives a label_id. It then inserts a row into numeric_series.series (label_id). The label_id is the stable identifier for the series.

internal_flow.name: measurement_write
internal_flow.description: For add and edit operations, the backend validates value (finite float) and recorded_at (ISO-8601). It upserts into numeric_series.measurements. Sparkline and latest value are always derived at read time — no materialized summary columns.

internal_flow.name: list_read
internal_flow.description: For the list view, the backend joins numeric_series.series with labels.labels on label_id to get names, then for each series queries the N most recent measurements for sparkline values and selects the single measurement with MAX(recorded_at) as the latest value. Result is sorted by label name ascending. sparkline_values is serialized as a JSON string (e.g. '[1.2, 3.4, 5.6]') in the Dataset row so that the ColumnType remains 'string'. The UI Implementer must parse this field in SeriesListPage; standard platform TableView must not be used for this surface.
outputs: Dataset: rows with {id=label_id (string), label_name (string), latest_value (number or null), sparkline_values (string, JSON-encoded float array)}

internal_flow.name: detail_read
internal_flow.description: For the detail view, the backend fetches all measurements for the given label_id ordered by recorded_at DESC. Returns as Dataset with schema {id, value, recorded_at}.

internal_flow.name: series_delete
internal_flow.description: Deletes all measurements for label_id then deletes the series record. The LabelEngine label is not deleted — it remains in LabelEngine's registry. The caller is responsible for not re-adding a series on the same label_id after deletion unless intended.

internal_flow.name: batch_read
internal_flow.description: Accepts a list of label_ids. The backend queries labels.labels directly for ALL requested label_ids (not only those in numeric_series.series) to retrieve label_name. For each label_id: if a series record exists in numeric_series.series, fetch all measurements; otherwise return an empty measurements array. A label_id that does not exist in labels.labels at all is included with label_name: null and empty measurements. Returns structured response (not Dataset) for external API contract.

internal_flow.name: external_write
internal_flow.description: Accepts label_id and a list of {value, recorded_at} entries. Validates each entry. Inserts all valid entries. Returns {inserted: int}. If label_id is not found in numeric_series.series, the behavior must be explicitly chosen before implementation (open question).

internal_required.role: Label creation and name lookup via HTTP API; label table read via shared Postgres schema
Shared Postgres instance for private application schema

external_required.name: httpx
external_required.role: HTTP client for LabelEngine API calls

forbidden: Any direct manipulation of the labels.labels or labels.object_labels tables beyond read-only join on label_id/name
Encoding units, health-domain, or composite metric logic in this slice
Materializing sparkline or latest_value as stored columns in this slice

deferred_decisions: Sparkline window size (N most recent values): implementer should choose a sensible default (e.g. 20) and surface as configuration if needed
Label name global uniqueness: LabelEngine enforces this — NumericSeries inherits whatever constraint LabelEngine applies; confirm with LabelEngine behavior before implementation
Soft-delete vs hard-delete for series: draft says delete removes history; hard delete is specified; implementer must verify this is acceptable

risks.risk: LabelEngine label and NumericSeries series are not atomically created
risks.impact: If LabelEngine create succeeds but NumericSeries insert fails, a label exists without a series. Retry by the user would fail on label name conflict. Mitigation: detect duplicate-name error from LabelEngine and treat as recovery path.

risks.risk: Sparkline derivation at read time may be slow with many series
risks.impact: List view latency increases linearly with series count. Acceptable for this slice per draft constraints. Will require re-evaluation if series count grows significantly.

risks.risk: Unknown-label behavior for external write is unresolved
risks.impact: Implementation cannot be completed for POST /api/series/{label_id}/values without an explicit product decision. Block on this before implementation.

open_questions.question: For the external write endpoint (OpenClaw), if the label_id does not exist in numeric_series.series, should it be rejected (404), auto-created (insert series record), or configurable?
Should label names be globally unique or can duplicates exist? LabelEngine controls this — implementer must verify LabelEngine's uniqueness constraint.
Should deleting a series be recoverable (soft delete) or permanent (hard delete)? Draft says delete removes history, implying hard delete.
Are measurements editable inline in the detail list, or through a per-row edit form?
Resolved: batch-read API returns full measurement history. No windowing in this slice.
